pages.title: Yasmine's Green World
text: She had grown up in a village on the side of a beautiful mountain, surrounded by oak forests, wildflowers, and a sparkling river.
She knew the songs of the birds.
And she loved running through the grass.
Then one day, her father came home with news.
His new job would take the family far away.
Before leaving, she collected seeds from some of her favorite flowers and tucked them carefully into a little bag.
She would take a piece of her green world with her.

pages.title: A Different Home
text: When Yasmine arrived at her new home, she looked around.
Near the house stood an old olive tree. Its branches were dry and tired, but it still offered a little shade.
But then she remembered the seeds in her little bag.
"If flowers grew there," she thought, "perhaps they can grow here too."
She chose a shady place beneath the old olive tree and planted them.
Water was precious in the desert.
So instead of wasting fresh water, Yasmine began saving suitable water that had already been used around the house.
Every afternoon, she carried her little jug to the olive tree.
She sprinkled a little water over the soil.

pages.title: Nothing
text: "Maybe nothing can grow here," Yasmine whispered.
She put down her little jug and walked home.

pages.title: Something Is Alive!
text: Several days later, Yasmine was playing ball with her brother.
And the ball rolled toward the old olive tree.
She forgot all about the ball.
Something green was pushing through the sand.
She raced home for her jug.
Every day the little plants grew taller.
But Yasmine soon discovered something strange.
These weren't the flowers she had brought from the mountain.
Her own seeds had never grown.
These plants had been here all along.
Their seeds had been sleeping beneath the desert soil.
Yasmine touched one of the yellow flowers.
"So the desert isn't empty after all."

pages.title: Yasmine's Little Garden
text: Yasmine collected seeds from the new flowers and planted them around the house.
Little by little, the patch beneath the olive tree changed.
Yasmine had tried to bring her old world to the desert.
Instead, the desert had introduced her to a world of its own.

pages.title: A New Voice
text: One spring morning, Yasmine woke to a strange sound.
It wasn't the chirping of the birds.
Her father followed her to the balcony.
"Don't be afraid, Yasmine. That's the cooing of a pigeon."
They looked toward the old olive tree.
There were two pigeons among its branches.
And they were carrying tiny twigs.
The tree that had once stood almost alone in the sand was becoming someone's home.

pages.title: Four Months
text: Four months had passed since Yasmine's family had arrived.
Her father had promised that every four months they would visit their old village.
But his work had become difficult.
This time, he knew he couldn't keep his promise.
He didn't know how to tell Yasmine.
"Come with me. I want to show you something."
They walked beyond their little garden and climbed a high dune.
Yasmine wondered if her father was about to talk about their journey home.
He lay back on the sand.
Then she forgot what she had been waiting to hear.

pages.title: A Sky Full of Stars
text: The sky was covered in stars.
They seemed scattered across the darkness like grains of wheat thrown across a field at planting time.
"It's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen!"
"The most beautiful? Even more beautiful than our mountain?"
"You know how much I love our oak forests."
She stretched out her arms beneath the enormous sky.
"It makes me feel so small… and the universe so big."
"You cannot see a sky like this everywhere."
"The desert isn't so bad, is it?"
He had not brought her here only to see the stars.

pages.title: The Night Visitor
text: A shape appeared between the dunes.
A graceful gazelle stepped into the moonlight.
But it wasn't running deeper into the desert.
The gazelle disappeared among the plants Yasmine had spent months caring for.
Yasmine jumped to her feet and ran down the dune.
"I'm going to ask it to stay during the day too!"
"I'll take care of it every day!"
Her father watched her racing toward the little patch of green.
There was no need to tell her what he had been afraid to say.

pages.title: Four New Friends
text: As Yasmine's little garden grew, her family brought home three chickens and a rooster.
Yasmine built them a small wooden shelter beneath the old olive tree.
Every day she brought them scraps from the kitchen and scattered grain over the ground.
Wherever the chickens scratched, the hard surface of the soil became loose and soft.
Yasmine began watching everything more carefully now.
There always seemed to be something happening that she had never noticed before.

pages.title: Goodbye
text: Yasmine's family had to leave for a week.
She filled their containers with grain.
She left them plenty of water.
"Don't eat everything on the first day," she warned them.

pages.title: The Tree Awakens
text: All week, Yasmine wondered about her chickens.
When the family finally returned, she jumped out and ran toward the coop.
Three hens came racing toward her.
Then she noticed something above her.
On the old olive tree was a branch she had never seen before.
The old tree was growing again.
Yasmine placed her hand against its trunk.

pages.title: The Stranger
text: One afternoon, Yasmine sat beneath the tree watching her chickens.
Then she heard a sound beyond the garden.
Something was moving across the empty land.
An old man was approaching with a walking stick.
Yasmine stepped behind the olive tree.
The stranger had a gentle face.
Behind him stood a goat tugging impatiently at a rope.
"Forgive me for disturbing you," the old man said. "I saw your home from far away. I wondered whether your chickens had left anything they wouldn't eat."
The goat buried her nose in them at once.
After that, the old man began visiting often.
Yasmine liked listening to his stories.
And the goat liked eating her leftovers.

pages.title: Thieves!
text: One morning Yasmine discovered a line of ants carrying away the chickens' grain.
Hundreds of tiny ants marched across the ground carrying seeds.
Yasmine fetched some water and poured it over the ants.
The water disappeared quickly into the tiny holes and tunnels.
The old man was standing behind her.
"They're stealing the chickens' food!" Yasmine protested.

pages.title: Look More Closely
text: At the end of the trail…
One of Yasmine's chickens was tearing excitedly at the soil.
"The ants eat some of your grain," said the old man.
"And sometimes your chickens eat the ants."
Then the old man pointed toward a patch of green in the distance.
Yasmine had noticed it before but had never thought much about it.
A little green island surrounded by desert.
"If it weren't for ants," the old man said, "that orchard might not be there."
The old man sat beneath the olive tree.

pages.title: The Village That Disappeared
text: "Long ago," he began, "this land wasn't like this."
The old man pointed across the desert.
"There was a village here surrounded by gardens and orchards."
Yasmine tried to imagine green fields where she could now see only sand.
"Some say the villagers left their farms and moved to the cities. With nobody caring for the land, the desert slowly swallowed it.
"Others say the land began drying first, forcing the people to leave."

pages.title: The Last Neighbor
text: Abu Numan was already an old man.
His children had moved to the city.
Most of his neighbors had gone.
Every evening, he walked through the nearly abandoned village with his two sheep until he reached what had once been his orchard.
Only a few weeds and thorny plants remained.
One afternoon, Abu Numan sat beneath a dried olive tree.
They hurried across the dusty ground searching for food.
Abu Numan felt sorry for them.
The next day, Abu Numan fed them again.

pages.title: The Ant Man
text: Abu Numan began collecting food scraps from the few remaining homes.
But the fierce desert sun dried them quickly.
So Abu Numan had an idea.
Then he loosely covered them with soil.
"The Ant Man!" they called Abu Numan.
When his children heard what he was doing, they became worried about him.
They came from the city and persuaded their father to leave the village and stay with them.
Abu Numan did not want to go.

pages.title: The Rain
text: Abu Numan wasn't happy in the city.
He missed the dead olive trees.
And rain fell over the old village.
Water rushed across the hard ground.
But where the ants had dug their tunnels, some water traveled deeper into the earth.
Away from the hot surface, moisture remained in the soil longer.
And deep underground, something was waiting.

pages.title: The Orchard Awakens
text: When spring came, Abu Numan returned to the village.
He stopped at the edge of his land.
Fresh shoots reached from branches everyone had thought were dead.
Abu Numan walked slowly among his trees.
The tiny creatures he had tried to help had, in their own way, helped his land.

pages.title: Abu Numan
text: For a moment, Yasmine said nothing.
She looked toward the green orchard.
Then back at the old man.
He picked up a handful of soil.
The earth trickled slowly through his fingers.
"I learned that the land was still alive."

pages.title: Yasmine's Idea
text: At the yellow flowers that had once slept beneath the soil.
At the olive tree growing new leaves.
At the pigeons nesting among its branches.
At the chickens scratching the earth.
At the ants vanishing into tiny tunnels.
She remembered the gazelle visiting at night.
All these months, Yasmine had thought she was creating a garden.
Now she understood that she wasn't doing it alone.
The next morning, she dug a small hole.
She put some food scraps inside.
The following day she dug another.
Abu Numan taught her what he had learned.
And Yasmine began watching the land more carefully than ever.

pages.title: Little by Little
text: The goat ate the larger scraps.
The ants carried tiny pieces underground.
The pigeons raised their young in the olive tree.
Other families began paying attention too.
They stopped seeing the land as empty.
They began caring for the soil.
They saved water when they could.
Little by little, patches of green appeared across the damaged land.
The desert landscape was still there, but where the land had been damaged and abandoned, life began returning.

pages.title: The Conqueror of the Desert
text: Years later, children played beneath the trees.
Some found it difficult to believe that parts of the land around their village had once been almost completely barren.
Yasmine told them about the yellow flowers that had surprised her beneath the old olive tree.
She told them about the pigeons.
And the tiny ants she had once called thieves.
But most of all, she told them about an old man who had once shared his food with a colony of hungry ants because he could not bear to see another living creature struggle alone.
The villagers never forgot Abu Numan.
And they gave him a name:
But whenever someone called him by that name, Abu Numan would laugh.
And somewhere nearby, Yasmine would smile.
The desert wasn't an enemy to conquer.
The land didn't need a conqueror.
It needed someone willing to look closely enough to discover what was still alive…
and patient enough to help it grow.
